Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A records office files incoming documents by indexing identifiers, routing dates, and custody fields into sequential ledgers, then distributes copies through internal mail and access-controlled archives; filings are retrievable by reference number and retain prior version stamps.

2) What occurred: The actor prepared an aircraft components ledger entry describing a substituted component under the original part number; altered the maintenance transaction log field for the affected airframe, recasting the entry date to a pre-installation date and removing the prior removal record; amended the component certificate of conformity field to reference the original supplier; routed the amended package through the internal maintenance approval channel under the supervisor's account; and transmitted the reconciled summary to the regulator filing channel on a date after the return-to-service inspection.

3) Materials/access observed: Aircraft components ledger entry (part number, serial, installation date fields); maintenance transaction log entry (work order reference, date stamp, technician identifier field); component certificate of conformity document (supplier name, issuance date fields); internal approval channel message under the supervisor's account; regulator filing channel transmission (filing reference number, submission date field).

4) Indicators & artifacts: Ledger entry with a serial number absent from the supplier's issuance records; log entry date earlier than the component's manufacture date in the certificate; certificate supplier name mismatched to the serial; approval channel message authored from an account inconsistent with the recorded technician; filing reference with a submission timestamp after the logged return-to-service inspection; version stamp on the ledger showing a second edit to the same record.
